installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Rust Dedicated Server + Carbon installer for Pterodactyl
# Server files: /mnt/server

set -euo pipefail

SRCDS_APPID=258550
SERVER_DIR="/mnt/server"
STEAMCMD_DIR="${SERVER_DIR}/steamcmd"

# Carbon's current Linux release archive.
CARBON_URL="${CARBON_URL:-https://github.com/CarbonCommunity/Carbon.Core/releases/latest/download/Carbon.Linux.Release.tar.gz}"

# Steam login is normally anonymous for Rust Dedicated Server.
STEAM_USER="${STEAM_USER:-anonymous}"
STEAM_PASS="${STEAM_PASS:-}"
STEAM_AUTH="${STEAM_AUTH:-}"

if [ "${STEAM_USER}" = "anonymous" ]; then
    echo "Using anonymous Steam login."
else
    echo "Using configured Steam account: ${STEAM_USER}"
fi

## Carbon folder from git, if configured. The clone itself happens at first boot
## (js/sections/carbon_git_sync.js): the runtime image ships git and ssh, and this
## install container can't reliably get ssh. It clones into an empty folder, so
## this script only moves the old folder aside and leaves Carbon to the boot update.
CARBON_GIT_URL="${CARBON_GIT_URL:-}"
MODDING_ROOT="${MODDING_ROOT:-carbon}"
USE_CARBON_GIT=0
if [ -n "${CARBON_GIT_URL}" ]; then
    case "$(echo "${FRAMEWORK:-}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
        *carbon*)
            if [[ "${MODDING_ROOT}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] && [ "${MODDING_ROOT}" != "." ] && [ "${MODDING_ROOT}" != ".." ]; then
                USE_CARBON_GIT=1
            else
                echo "WARNING: MODDING_ROOT '${MODDING_ROOT}' must be a single folder name to use git. Ignoring CARBON_GIT_URL."
            fi
            ;;
        *) echo "WARNING: CARBON_GIT_URL is set but the framework is not Carbon. Ignoring it." ;;
    esac
fi

echo "Preparing directories..."
mkdir -p "${SERVER_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${STEAMCMD_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${SERVER_DIR}/steamapps"

echo "Downloading SteamCMD..."
cd /tmp
curl -fsSL \
    -o steamcmd.tar.gz \
    https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz

tar -xzf steamcmd.tar.gz -C "${STEAMCMD_DIR}"
rm -f steamcmd.tar.gz

# SteamCMD can fail with a disk-write error if this does not exist.
mkdir -p "${SERVER_DIR}/steamapps"

# Pterodactyl normally expects this ownership at the end.
# SteamCMD sometimes needs root ownership during install in this setup.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME="${SERVER_DIR}"

echo "Installing/updating Rust Dedicated Server..."
cd "${STEAMCMD_DIR}"

./steamcmd.sh \
    +force_install_dir "${SERVER_DIR}" \
    +login "${STEAM_USER}" "${STEAM_PASS}" "${STEAM_AUTH}" \
    +app_update "${SRCDS_APPID}" validate \
    +quit

if [ "${USE_CARBON_GIT}" = "1" ]; then
    # Only reached once the game install succeeded, so a failed install keeps the old folder.
    CARBON_DIR="${SERVER_DIR}/${MODDING_ROOT}"
    if [ -d "${CARBON_DIR}" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "${CARBON_DIR}")" ]; then
        CARBON_BACKUP="${CARBON_DIR}.old-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
        echo "Moving existing ${MODDING_ROOT} folder to ${CARBON_BACKUP##*/}. Delete it once you no longer need it."
        mv "${CARBON_DIR}" "${CARBON_BACKUP}"
    fi
    echo "${MODDING_ROOT} folder will be cloned from git, and Carbon installed, on first boot."
else
    echo "Installing/updating Carbon..."
    cd "${SERVER_DIR}"

    rm -f /tmp/Carbon.Linux.Release.tar.gz

    curl -fsSL \
        -o /tmp/Carbon.Linux.Release.tar.gz \
        "${CARBON_URL}"

    tar -xzf /tmp/Carbon.Linux.Release.tar.gz -C "${SERVER_DIR}"
    rm -f /tmp/Carbon.Linux.Release.tar.gz
fi

echo "Setting up Steam client compatibility libraries..."
mkdir -p "${SERVER_DIR}/.steam/sdk32"
mkdir -p "${SERVER_DIR}/.steam/sdk64"

cp -fv "${STEAMCMD_DIR}/linux32/steamclient.so" \
    "${SERVER_DIR}/.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so"

cp -fv "${STEAMCMD_DIR}/linux64/steamclient.so" \
    "${SERVER_DIR}/.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so"

echo "Rust Dedicated Server and Carbon installation completed."

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name of your server in the public server list.

variables.name: Description
variables.description: The description under your server title. Commonly used for rules & info. Use \n for newlines.

variables.name: URL
variables.description: The URL for your server. This is what comes up when clicking the "Visit Website" button.

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: The maximum amount of players allowed in the server at once.

variables.name: Server Image
variables.description: The header image for the top of your server listing.

variables.name: RCON Port
variables.description: Port for RCON connections.

variables.name: RCON Password
variables.description: RCON access password. Using a weak password will cause the server to not start. Set a strong password. You can generate a strong password here: https://randomkeygen.com/

variables.name: Save Interval
variables.description: Sets the server’s auto-save interval in seconds.

variables.name: Additional Arguments
variables.description: Add additional startup parameters to the server.

variables.name: App Port
variables.description: Port for the Rust+ App. -1 to disable.

variables.name: Server Logo
variables.description: The circular server logo for the Rust+ app.

variables.name: Custom Map URL
variables.description: Overwrites the map with the one from the direct download URL. Invalid URLs will cause the server to crash.

variables.name: Level
variables.description: The world file for Rust to use.

variables.name: World Size
variables.description: The world size for a procedural map.

variables.name: World Seed
variables.description: The seed for a procedural map.

variables.name: Query Port
variables.description: Server Query Port. Can't be the same as Game's primary port.

variables.name: Modding Framework
variables.description:
The modding framework to be used: carbon, oxide, vanilla.
Defaults to "vanilla" for a non-modded server installation.

variables.name: Version
variables.description: Choose which beta version to use for your server. Public is the current version of Rust and should be used for live servers unless you're running a staging server of some sort.

variables.name: Modding Root Directory
variables.description: The root directory of your modding framework - If using carbon, this should be set to carbon. If using oxide, this should've set to oxide.

variables.name: Server Tags
variables.description: Server tags allow your server to be categorized. There is a list below of all tags. Separate each tag with a comma such as: weekly,NA,vanilla | All available server tags are listed here: https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/server-browser-tags

variables.name: Server Identity
variables.description: The directory of your server. Default is set to rust.

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Determines if the server with automatically update on start.

variables.name: Chaos Code Extension
variables.description: Download and use the ChaosCode extension?

variables.name: Discord Extension
variables.description: Download and use the Discord Extension?

variables.name: RustEdit Extension
variables.description: Download and install the RustEdit Extension?

variables.name: Validate Game Files
variables.description: Determine if you want the server to validate the game files every time the server starts.

variables.name: App Public IP
variables.description: Unless you know what you're doing, leave this field blank. This is very important! Please do not change this unless you have read the Rust+ App documentation here: https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/rust-companion-server

variables.name: Framework Update
variables.description: Disable installation / update of any chosen framework.

variables.name: Gamemode
variables.description: Gamemode of Rust - Choose between none (default),vanilla,survival,softcore,hardcore

variables.name: Log File Location
variables.description: Choose a location to log your console outputs. Leave blank to disable.

variables.name: Debug Mode
variables.description: Do you want to enable the egg's debug mode?

variables.name: Mono Logging
variables.description: Outputs all mono logs to a file. This is a developer only tool to troubleshoot and should not be ran in a production server. Outputs are logged into mono-debug.log as well as the Pterodactyl terminal.

variables.name: Carbon Git URL
variables.description: Repository holding the Carbon folder, e.g. git@github.com:you/carbon.git. Leave empty to disable. It is cloned on first boot after a reinstall, and the old folder is moved to a timestamped backup. Requires Framework Update to be on. Tracked files are reset to the repository on every boot.

variables.name: Carbon Git Branch
variables.description: Branch to use. Leave empty for the repository's default branch.

variables.name: Carbon Git Private Key
variables.description: SSH private key for the repository; use a read-only deploy key. Paste it with line breaks flattened to spaces or as \n, base64-encode it, or give a file path under /home/container. Leave empty for public repositories.
